note: Proposed risk cases for the verification campaign, one list per console, in priority order. Titles are matched against the file names of the ROM folder (region and revision tags ignored, USA/World/Europe preferred); arcade sets are matched by set name. A case missing from the folder is listed as unmatched and skipped. Reasons come from the repository documents named in 'source'; a case is a place where the converter is known to be harder to satisfy or to refuse, not a promise that it passes. 'expect': 'refusal' marks a case where the documented outcome is a clean refusal of the cartridge. Trimmed with Arthur on 27 Oct 2026: about half of each list, five at most, plus two random games per console (select --random 2).

gg.title: Streets of Rage II

gb.title: Tetris

gb.title: Pokemon - Red Version

gb.title: Super Mario Land

gb.title: Lazlos' Leap

gb.title: Donkey Kong Land
gb.reason: Reported RAM fallback remained on the longer probes; the converter should keep reducing it

nes.title: Castlevania III - Dracula's Curse
nes.reason: Mapper 5 (MMC5) with mapped RAM; 0 percent fallback in the 9 October qualification

nes.title: Legend of Zelda, The
nes.reason: MMC1; the largest fallback of its qualification (2.91 percent) sits in the cartridge address range below $8000

nes.title: Esper Dream 2

md.title: Sonic The Hedgehog 2

md.title: Ecco the Dolphin
md.reason: 68000 code runs from RAM through an interrupt stub using TRAP #0; the case that exposed the TRAP translation

md.title: NBA Jam - Tournament Edition
md.reason: Acclaim serial EEPROM board (24C02 family) with persistence and F8/F9 busy-write states

md.title: Super Street Fighter II
md.reason: 5 MiB cartridge with the Sega 512 KiB bank-mapping circuit (MK-12056), the declared banked-ROM case

md.title: Gunstar Heroes
md.reason: Heavy Z80 sound driver and a Japan region lock; zero Z80 fallback is part of its documented result

snes.title: Star Fox
snes.reason: Super Fox GSU (MARIO chip) with an old header, 64 KiB RAM by default; GSU instructions are counted apart from the 65816

snes.title: Super Mario World 2 - Yoshi's Island
snes.reason: GSU-2 with 2 MiB ROM and battery RAM

snes.title: Pilotwings
snes.reason: DSP-1 board; exposed the missing raster and projection commands

snes.title: Mega Man X2
snes.reason: CX4 board; CX4 instructions stay interpreted and are reported on their own device line

snes.title: Super Mario RPG - Legend of the Seven Stars
snes.reason: SA-1 board (second 65816, BW-RAM, mailbox and IRQ with the S-CPU): a counted interpreted device since 1.6.6; the reference case of the SA-1 work

ng.title: Metal Slug 3
ng.reason: Its crab-scene state is the reference for the Neo Geo state-ABI migration

ng.title: The King of Fighters 2003
ng.reason: PVC protection RAM (520,517-byte states); its first replay failed in the campaign that exposed the PVC state

ng.title: Garou: Mark of the Wolves
ng.reason: SMA protected board of the 14 October protection work

ng.title: The King of Fighters '98
ng.reason: KOF '98 mapping family with its own code view and state extension

ng.title: Twinkle Star Sprites
ng.reason: Enhanced-mode route; reached 42 uncompiled cartridge entries before the correction

cps1.title: Street Fighter II': Champion Edition
cps1.reason: Runs part of its code from graphics RAM, which native code does not cover: 75,546 interpreted instructions (0.06 percent)

cps1.title: Final Fight
cps1.reason: Gave the same route hashes on Windows and Debian 13; the Windows/Debian witness

cps1.title: Captain Commando
cps1.reason: Four players; attract mode compared pixel for pixel with MAME

cps1.title: Strider
cps1.reason: Compared with MAME 0.289 pixel for pixel on attract and credited play

cps1.title: Warriors of Fate
cps1.reason: QSound board (CPS-1.5): Kabuki-encrypted Z80, serial EEPROM, QSound (high-level model) from the player's own DSP ROM; the experimental tier, its reports say so

cps2.title: Super Street Fighter II: The New Challengers
cps2.reason: Raster interrupt in its attract demonstration from frame 6,818; six buttons

cps2.title: Dungeons & Dragons: Tower of Doom
cps2.reason: Four players on a blank EEPROM; the only panel set above two players

cps2.title: Dungeons & Dragons: Shadow over Mystara
cps2.reason: Starts as a two-player board on a blank EEPROM: players 3 and 4 need the service switch and the test menu

cps2.title: Marvel Super Heroes
cps2.reason: Selects a QSound sound bank above 5, which the quick-state loader once refused

cps2.title: Mars Matrix
cps2.reason: Reads the raster counter next to a line boundary: its title animation runs one frame ahead of MAME's for frames 775 to 783

x68.title: Metal Sight (System Sacom)
x68.reason: Five-disk set whose disk changes follow the game's own requests

x68.title: Lemmings (Imagineer)
x68.reason: Mouse game that drives the SCC mouse channel itself

x68.title: Super Hang-On
x68.reason: Two-disk set that ejects its disks after loading; must run exactly as without the policy

pce.title: Bonk's Adventure
pce.reason: Control case: 0 interpreted instructions on its routes; the play route needs two Run presses because a third pauses the game

pce.title: Street Fighter II' - Champion Edition
pce.reason: 2.5 MiB board with 466 bank contexts: needs more than 65,536 instruction identities, so it takes the engine's larger capture format (734,635 emitted); a 25 MB game and a long conversion, and whatever passes 1,048,576 is left out and counted

pce.title: Bomberman '93
pce.reason: Multitap game: a converted game is built for two players (the help text says so), the four-seat build is not offered and neither is the fifth multitap player

pce.title: Dai Makaimura
pce.reason: SuperGrafx game: one video chip only shows no picture, so the conversion must refuse it

pce.title: Space Harrier
pce.reason: Attract loop with no input stops changing after a few frames; the play route must still move

amiga.title: Lotus 2
amiga.reason: Control case and the test game: 0 interpreted instructions on its three routes of the extended level, a 3D road and colour steps

amiga.title: Another World
amiga.reason: Needs the player's Kickstart; its routes answer the code wheel with the joystick and leave the mouse out, because the install turns a left click into the access-code screen, which locks a game whose protection has not passed

amiga.title: Pinball Dreams
amiga.reason: NTSC install whose keys choose the table: the long route plays one table natively, and three of the four tables run partly on the counted interpreter (Ignition about half)

amiga.title: Lemmings
amiga.reason: Mouse game: its routes wait for the intro, move the pointer onto 1 PLAYER and click; generic inputs during the intro shorten it and click where no button is

amiga.title: Superfrog
amiga.reason: The archive holds no WHDLoad slave: not an Amiga WHDLoad install, so the conversion must refuse it with its sentence

atarist.title: Bomb Jack
atarist.reason: Control case of the panel of eight: EmuTOS, starts by itself, one disk, a joystick game; 5 interpreted instructions on its routes (the start of EmuTOS)

atarist.title: Operation Stealth
atarist.reason: Three disks started by the desktop (Hatari's GEMDOS hook runs on the interpreter) and a colour-code protection that the routes stop on, with the reason in route_warnings

atarist.title: Turrican II
atarist.reason: Stops on EmuTOS (listed in EmuTOS's own incompatibility notes): the player's own TOS 1.04 is chosen in Options > Atari ST, and then it has 0 interpreted instructions on its routes

atarist.title: The Lurking Horror
atarist.reason: Writes 27 sectors to its own disk by GEMDOS when it saves, and runs about 99,000 instructions on the interpreter on its main route (the most of the panel): the saves are kept beside the quick state and a new process finds them

atarist.title: Another World
atarist.reason: Two disks and a code-wheel protection: the routes end on the game's own check (a screen that says ERROR) and the report says so; the converter never answers or skips a protection

msx.title: Knightmare - Majou Densetsu
msx.reason: Control case: plain 32 KiB cartridge, 0 interpreted instructions on its routes under C-BIOS

msx.title: Spy vs Spy II - The Island Caper
msx.reason: PAL cartridge whose bytes suggest ASCII 16; the probe runs choose Konami SCC, which the game drives

msx.title: Dragon Slayer II - Xanadu
msx.reason: ASCII 8 with 8 KiB battery SRAM: the SRAM bit is found from the bank values the game writes, then the save must survive a fresh process

msx.title: Deep Dungeon
msx.reason: ASCII 8 with 2 KiB battery SRAM: the mapper probe read it as ASCII 16 until writes to the SRAM were counted apart (14 November 2026)

msx.title: Salamander
msx.reason: Konami SCC; its playfield was once seen black under C-BIOS in development, then drawn on the panel's routes

msx2.title: Space Manbow
msx2.reason: Konami SCC and the V9938's vertical scroll; the owner saw the scroll judder before 1.7.3

msx2.title: Aleste
msx2.reason: Its bytes suggest Konami SCC, whose probe run falls into an empty slot; ASCII 16 is chosen

msx2.title: Super Daisenryaku
msx2.reason: ASCII 16 with 2 KiB battery SRAM that looks for an FM-PAC in the other slots; read as ASCII 8 until one register write stopped counting as evidence (14 November 2026)

msx2.title: Hydlide 3 - The Space Memories
msx2.reason: ASCII 8 role-playing game whose routes stayed in its character set-up menu at the extended level

msx2.title: Metal Gear
msx2.reason: Konami; the play route stops at the first transceiver call, the long route goes on
